title: How to Skew Correct a Six-Sided Die
content:
## Introduction
A method for skew-correcting a six-sided die can be found in the "A generalization to loaded dice" section within the article located at https://pit-claudel.fr/clement/blog/generating-uniformly-random-data-from-skewed-input-biased-coins-loaded-dice-skew-correction-and-the-von-neumann-extractor/



**This** particular article will use a worked example to *mathematically guarantee* 128 bits (for a 12 word seed phrease) or 256 bits (for a 24 word seed phrase) of entropy using a 6-sided die (d6). A big thank you to Discord member Couyon for starting this discussion at Roll your 3-dice sequences, discard sequences with more than one of the same number, find the sequence below to map the number. Then SHA256 the rolls directly or (optionally) map your bits (evens & odds or 1-3 + 4-6)

In this article we will create a **12 word seed phrase**. Therefore we will need a total of **50** d6 values. These values are obtained by mapping sequences of triplet rolls according to their *order*:

```LMH=1, LHM=2, MHL=3, MLH=6, HLM=5, HML=4```

where L=Low, M=Middle, H=High. For example, the sequence 123 is in the order LMH. But so are all these other triplets:

``123, 124, 125, 126, 234, 235, 236, 345, 346, 456``

The premise behind this is that there are 3!=6 different ways to arrange the letters "L, M, H" and therefore can map all sequences to the numbers on a six-sided die.

The process is summarized below:

1) Roll a single six-sided die (d6) three times and record its values
2) Any triplet with distinct values is kept and mapped to the orderings described above (LMH, LHM, ...); any triplet with at least two of the same values is discarded
3) Repeat until we obtain 50 d6 values

## A Small Example: 10 Trials

We will use 10 trials as a starting point. Let's say we rolled a d6 die three times and repeated this process 10 times to get the series of rolls

```123 463 244 152 236 654 411 614 614 336```

This gives us ten sequences of three digits. Any repeated digits within a sequence is discarded and the rest are mapped to one of the orderings.

```LMH MHL X LHM LMH HML X HLM HLM X```

Now the remaining are mapped to either 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 according to the ordering maps above:

```LMH=1 MHL=3 X LHM=2 LMH=1 HML=4 X HLM=5 HLM=5 X```

Therefore out of 10 trials, we have obtained the 7 die rolls

```1 3 2 1 4 5 5```

*(Note we expect around 45% of these triplets to get discarded)*

## A Big Example: 50 D6 Values

Let's assume we have continued this process until we have 50 rolls in total. Let's use this example:

```136, 235, 425, 512, 124, 432, 523, 456, 456, 652, 532, 431, 651, 643, 314, 361, 145, 162, 145, 265, 365, 641, 143, 532, 531, 541, 146, 614, 461, 364, 126, 324, 256, 216, 214, 231, 126, 325, 524, 541, 265, 326, 436, 416, 634, 631, 461, 245, 356, 352```

which has orderings

```LMH, LMH, MLH, HLM, LMH, HML, HLM, LMH, LMH, HML, HML, HML, HML, HML, MLH, MHL, LMH, LHM, LMH, LHM, LHM, HML, LHM, HML, HML, HML, LMH, HLM, MHL, LHM, LMH, MLH, LMH, MLH, MLH, MHL, LMH, MLH, HLM, HML, LHM, MLH, MLH, MLH, HLM, HML, MHL, LMH, LMH, MHL```

which maps to the die values

```    1, 1, 6, 5, 1, 4, 5, 1, 1, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 6, 3, 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 4, 2, 4, 4, 4, 1, 5, 3, 2, 1, 6, 1, 6, 6, 3, 1, 6, 5, 4, 2, 6, 6, 6, 5, 4, 3, 1, 1, 3```
